about.title: La Palma Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision changes everything, and it happens more often than most La Palma residents realize. Orange County's public crash records show that even a small city like La Palma, with under 16,000 residents, recorded a traffic death alongside dozens of injury collisions in the most recent year on file. Corridors such as La Palma Avenue, Walker Street, and Orangethorpe Avenue see the heaviest volume, with Thursday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. showing up often in the data. If a crash on one of these roads took a spouse, parent, or child, California law gives certain family members and dependents the right to pursue a wrongful death claim, separate from anything that happens in criminal court. Our team handles these claims directly and can explain what applies to your family's situation and help you move forward at your own pace.

whyChoose.title: Why La Palma Families Choose Us

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to spouses, domestic partners, and children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in certain situations. We can help clarify where your family stands before any deadline passes.

items.title: A Real Deadline That Doesn't Wait
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks significantly if a government entity was involved, such as a city road defect. Acting early preserves evidence and options.

items.title: Losses the Law Recognizes
items.desc: California allows families to recover funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and compensation for the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. We can help document these losses accurately.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim after a crash in La Palma?
items.answer: Generally, California gives families two years from the date of death to file a civil wrongful death claim. If the crash involved a government-owned road or vehicle, the deadline is much shorter, often just months, so it's worth speaking with us as soon as you're able.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring this kind of claim?
items.answer: California law prioritizes a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children to file first. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing depending on the family's circumstances. We can review your specific situation and explain who qualifies.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim connected to any criminal charges against the driver?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal prosecution the driver might face. The two proceedings run independently, and a family can pursue a civil claim regardless of the criminal outcome. This distinction matters especially on higher-volume roads like La Palma Avenue or Walker Street, where crash investigations can take time.

items.question: What kinds of losses can our family recover in La Palma?
items.answer: California law allows recovery for funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Every family's losses look different, and we can help explain how these categories might apply to your case.
